plan: This is a second-price auction, meaning the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value: bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win, while bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions unnecessarily. Since my value is $15, I will bid $15 to ensure I capture positive profit whenever the second-highest bid is below my value, without overpaying.

This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth if others bid between my value and my bid, while bidding lower reduces my chance of winning profitable auctions without any benefit. Since I pay the second-highest bid regardless of how high I bid above that, I should simply bid exactly my true value of $36 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no benefit to bidding above or below my true value of $42. Bidding exactly $42 ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than what I'd pay, and I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. This maximizes my expected profit.
